extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, examiners, and IP practitioners in the Philippines
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing rules and regulations governing filing, examination, grant, and post-grant/registration procedures for patents, utility models, and industrial designs in the Philippines (IPOPHL). Covers substantive patentability standards, formal requirements, drawing/sequence/claim standards, priority/filing rules, procedures for adverse information, registrability reports, correspondence, fees, and related administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any technical solution of a problem in any field of human activity which is new, involves an inventive step and is industrially applicable shall be patentable (Sec. 21, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability is assessed on novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness to a person skilled in the art), and industrial applicability. See related rules on novelty, prior art, inventive step, and industrial applicability for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory classes of patentable inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentable invention may be or may relate to: (a) a product (machine, device, article of manufacture, composition of matter, microorganism); (b) a process (method of use, manufacturing, non-biological or microbiological process); (c) computer-related inventions; and (d) an improvement of any of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject-matter eligibility follows these categories; specifics (e.g., computer-related inventions) are recognized as statutory classes rather than automatically excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are excluded from patent protection: discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, laws of nature, abstract ideas, schemes/rules/methods of mental acts or playing games, business methods without technical means, programs for computers, surgical/therapeutic/diagnostic methods practiced on the human/animal body (products for use in such methods excluded), plant varieties/animal breeds/essentially biological processes for production of plants/animals (microorganisms and non-biological/microbiological processes excepted), aesthetic creations, and anything contrary to public order/health/welfare/morality (e.g., cloning or germ-line modification, uses of the human embryo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists explicit exclusions; some exceptions (e.g., products for use in treatment) are noted. Refer to statutory and implementing rules where overlaps arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (newness) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall not be considered new if it forms part of the prior art (Sec. 23, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 204 for detailed definition of prior art. Novelty requires absence of any single prior art disclosure that anticipates the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art consists of: (a) everything made available to the public anywhere by written/oral disclosure, by use, or any other way before the filing or priority date; (b) whole contents of earlier applications published by IPOPHL filed/effective in the Philippines earlier than the filing/priority date (subject to common applicant/inventor rules); (c) whole contents of corresponding foreign applications published before the filing date disclosing substantially the same invention; (d) where multiple independent filings exist, contents of earliest filed application published on/after a later application's filing date can destroy novelty of the later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public availability is non-confidential/restricted disclosures. Prior use and oral disclosures must be proven with substantial evidence. 'Substantially the same' defined by composition of all important particulars, excluding formal/minor variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty strict identity test (equivalents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strict identity test is required in assessing novelty: a single prior art reference must disclose each and every element of a claimed invention to destroy novelty. Equivalents are considered only in assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on equivalents to defeat novelty; equivalents may be used when assessing obviousness/inventive step only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure (12-month grace provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of information contained in the application during the 12 months preceding the filing or priority date shall not prejudice the applicant on the ground of lack of novelty if such disclosure was made by: (a) the inventor or any person who had the right to the patent; (b) a foreign patent office, the Bureau or the Office under certain circumstances (another application filed by the inventor that should not have been disclosed or an application filed without inventor's knowledge/consent by a third party who obtained the information from the inventor); or (c) a third party who obtained the information directly or indirectly from the inventor. Applications published by foreign patent offices and WIPO are excluded from this protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a limited grace period tied to disclosures originating from the inventor or certain official sources; foreign office publications (and WIPO-published PCT apps) are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art, it is not obvious to a 'person skilled in the art' at the filing or priority date (Sec. 26, IP Code). Only prior art made available to the public before the filing/priority date shall be considered in assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the person skilled in the art standard; combine only publicly available references. See Rule 207 for presumed capabilities of that person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person having ordinary skills in the art (PHOSITA) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The person having ordinary skills in the art is presumed to be an ordinary practitioner aware of common general knowledge at the relevant date, to have knowledge of references sufficiently related to the pertinent art, and of arts reasonably pertinent to the inventor's problem; and to have normal means and capacity for routine work and experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this presumption when applying the inventive step test; consider what such a person would combine or find obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention that can be produced and used in any industry shall be industrially applicable (Sec. 27, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If industrial applicability is not obvious from the disclosure, an explicit indication must be provided in the application (see Rule 407(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to a patent (ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to a patent belongs to the inventor, his heirs, or assigns. When two or more persons jointly made an invention, the right belongs to them jointly (Sec. 28, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership rules follow inventorship; assignments and transfers affect who may apply or be named as applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be named as applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may be filed by the actual inventor(s) or in the name of his heirs, legal representatives, or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure correct naming to avoid later title disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of commissioned inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who commissions the work shall own the patent, unless otherwise provided in the contract (Sec. 30.1, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual provisions can override default ownership rules; parties should have clear agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee inventions (course of employment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inventive activity is not part of an employee's regular duties, the employee owns the patent even if employer resources used; if the invention results from the performance of regularly-assigned duties, the employer owns the patent unless agreement states otherwise (Sec. 30.2, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment contracts and job descriptions materially affect ownership; include express clauses if different allocation desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file principle
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more persons made the same invention independently, the right to the patent belongs to the person who filed an application, or to the applicant with the earliest filing or priority date. If filing/priority dates are identical, the time of day is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages prompt filing; earliest filing date (or priority) is determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority (Paris Convention claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed in the Philippines by a person who previously applied for the same invention in another treaty country shall be considered filed as of the foreign filing date provided: (a) the local application expressly claims priority; (b) it is filed within 12 months of the earliest foreign filing; and (c) a certified copy of the foreign application with English translation is filed within 6 months of filing in the Philippines. The 6-month period may be extended by Director for up to another 6 months for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply strictly with claim, timing, certified copy and translation requirements to preserve priority rights; Director may extend certified copy deadline upon good cause or treaty compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: An application can claim more than one priority, even from different countries. If multiple priorities are claimed, time limits computed from priority date use the earliest priority date; the local application and priority applications must have common inventor(s)/applicant(s). A fee for multiple priority claims is payable upon filing the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority coverage is limited to technical features included in the application(s) whose priority is claimed (Rule 306.1). Priority may be granted for features disclosed in the earlier application even if not previously claimed (Rule 306.2). If earlier priority could have been claimed but was not, applicant has 2 months from filing date to submit the priority claim with a declaration of unintentional delay and full fee payment (Rule 306.3). Failure to submit within time treats application as having no such claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy of foreign priority application
rubrics_metrics.description: The certified copy of the foreign application is the copy of the priority application certified as a true reproduction by the patent office which received it or any other office with official custody of the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certified documents are properly authenticated; translations required where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and channels for patent application filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be in writing, may be in Filipino or English, and shall be filed through: (a) IPOPHL electronic filing system; (b) electronic format or internet (e.g., email), if available; (c) post, mail, or courier (subject to fees) for voluminous applications only; or (d) Intellectual Property Satellite Offices (IPSOs) (subject to fees). All applications shall be addressed to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is mandatory except for voluminous invention applications (>250 pages) which may be filed manually. Follow channel-specific requirements and potential additional fees for paper submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall contain: (a) a duly accomplished request for grant of patent; (b) an abstract; (c) a description; (d) at least one claim; (e) drawings, if necessary; (f) payment of required fees at time of filing; and (g) appointment of agent/representative if applicant is non-resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper-based documents must be in two copies (except request for registration). Ensure all items are present to be accorded a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is subject to full payment of the filing fee and the publication fee (1st publication) upon filing. Priority claim fee is due upon filing when priority is claimed at filing; priority claims filed later within two months are subject to payment at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment of required fees at filing leads to failed application status (Rule 401.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of required fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be considered bona fide if required fees are not paid in full upon filing and will be deemed a failed application. The applicant may retrieve it by formal written request within 4 months from mailing date of notice of failed application; otherwise it will be expunged. A failed application due to non-payment shall not be published and may be filed anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly pay all required fees to avoid loss of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking of documents and acknowledgement; filing date criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall tag documents with the date of receipt and issue an acknowledgement stating application number, date of receipt, applicant name, and title. An application is accorded a filing date only if the Examiner determines the application is complete and contains all requirements in Rule 400. If incomplete, the Examiner issues an Office Action to address completeness for filing date purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness at examination matters for filing date. Ensure all required fields and items are present to secure filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard application form (request)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for grant shall be made on a form drawn up by the Office; a standard application form will be made available and may be reproduced by applicants at their own cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Office's form for the request to ensure compliance with formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the request (application header fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall contain petition for grant, applicant's name, mailing address with zip code, phone/mobile/email if no resident agent, title of invention, inventor's name(s), convention priority information if any (file number, country, date), resident agent contact if any, signature of applicant or agent, and other information required by law/rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate identity/contact and priority information to avoid procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure/description sufficiency (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person having ordinary skills in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the enabling disclosure test (Rule 406); include working examples where appropriate to show at least one way of doing the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for enabling disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The test is whether the person to whom the disclosure is addressed could, by following the directions therein, put the invention into practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical reproducibility by PHOSITA is required; mere theoretical statements insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enabling disclosure particulars (including chemicals/pharmaceuticals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enabling disclosure must contain clear and detailed description of at least one way of doing the invention using working examples; sufficient and clear disclosure of technical features including manner/process of making, performing, and using the invention, leaving nothing to conjecture. For chemical substances and pharmaceutical subject matter, include representative embodiments/working examples, pharmacological test results (for pharmaceuticals), and claimed activity for all compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For biotech/pharma, include experimental data and representative compounds/activities to satisfy enablement and support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must include: (a) technical field; (b) background art useful for understanding and examination (preferably cite documents); (c) summary of the invention in terms such that the technical problem and solution and advantageous effects are understood; (d) brief description of figures; (e) detailed description pointing out novel/inventive features relative to prior art with reference signs; (f) examples describing at least one way of carrying out the invention (referring to drawings where appropriate); (g) explicit indication of industrial applicability when not obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions should enable search and examination; tie claims to description and include examples and references to prior art where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for biological materials/microorganisms (disclosure and deposit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application concerns a microbiological process or product using a microorganism not publicly available or not sufficiently disclosed, the invention is regarded as disclosed only if: (a) a culture of the microorganism has been deposited in a depositary institution before filing; (b) the depositary institution and file number are stated (or submitted within two months of Examiner request); and (c) the application as filed gives relevant available information on characteristics of the microorganism. Publication is held pending until submission of deposit information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deposit in recognized depository and timely provision of deposit details to avoid publication/enablement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-allowance requirements for novel microorganism strains
rubrics_metrics.description: An application involving any novel strain must satisfy: (a) deposit in a recognized international or Philippine depositary authority guaranteeing viability for patent term; (b) proof of deposit with identification/deposit number; (c) depositary contractual obligation to place culture in permanent collection and provide access relevant to published patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect allowance until proper deposit and proof provided; choose approved depositaries and collect required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The title shall be as short and specific as possible, appearing as a heading on first page of description; must be in technical terms referring to technical features; fancy names not permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise technical descriptors that reflect the invention's technical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must be on a separate sheet with heading 'Abstract' and commence with the Title. It must be a concise summary of the disclosure in description, claims and drawings, preferably not more than 150 words, drafted to allow clear understanding of the technical problem, gist of the solution, and principal use(s). The abstract serves only for technical information and as an efficient basis for search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstracts concise (~150 words), focused on technical problem and solution; avoid including matter outside disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited matter in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall not contain: (i) statements contrary to public order or morality; (ii) statements disparaging other persons' products/processes/patents (mere comparison with prior art is not disparaging per se); (iii) statements obviously irrelevant or unnecessary. If present, the Office shall omit such matter in publication indicating place/number of words omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inflammatory, irrelevant, or defamatory statements; unnecessary material may be redacted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requisites for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be signed by the applicant or attorney/agent name may appear, show every feature covered by claims, may consist of several views with consecutive numbering, and each figure must be briefly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings illustrate claimed features clearly and correspond with description and reference signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform standard and strict requirements for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings must conform to a uniform standard of excellence suited for clear visualization; strict rules enforced and departures cause examination delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow all drawing rules to avoid delays; employ competent draftsman if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing paper, ink, and online drawing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually filed drawings must be on smooth non-glossy white paper permitting India ink erasures; only black India ink or equivalent used; white pigments to cover lines not permissible. Online drawings must be clear with black lines on white background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid colored inks or white-out; digital submissions must maintain high-contrast black-on-white clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing size and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings on A4 (29.7 x 21 cm) paper; minimum margins: top 5.5 cm, left 2.5 cm, right 1.5 cm, bottom 1 cm. All drawings, figure numbers, reference numerals and signatures must be within margins. Sheets numbered sequentially with 'sheet_number/total_sheets' format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow margin and numbering conventions to ensure acceptability and consistent reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing line quality, shading and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings executed with instruments giving satisfactory reproduction; durable, black, dense, uniformly thick well-defined lines without colors. Surface shading open; cross-sections by oblique hatching avoiding obscuring reference signs. Use fewest lines consistent with clarity; shading sparingly; assume light from upper-left at 45 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid heavy or crowded lines and excessive shading; ensure clarity after reductions (photographic reduction to two-thirds must still show details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale, composition and assembly of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale must be large enough for clear presentation without crowding; multiple sheets allowed only when necessary; figures forming a single complete figure across sheets must be arranged so complete figure can be assembled without concealment. Scale if given must be represented graphically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design drawings so that reduction/assembly does not obscure details; use multiple sheets only when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters/numerals and their presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views consecutively numbered; letters and figures of reference should measure at least 3.2 mm so they remain legible when reduced to 1.06 mm; placed to avoid interfering with comprehension; should not be placed on shaded surfaces and must be simple and clear (no brackets, circles or inverted commas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent use of reference signs across description/drawings; maintain legibility after reduction and avoid clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature placement on drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's name and signature or that of authorized representative should be placed at lower right-hand corner within margins and must not trespass upon drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place signatures within designated area to avoid obscuring figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning of large views and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Different figures arranged on sheets without wasting space, preferably upright. Views longer than sheet width may be presented sideways with top at left side of sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange to maximize clarity and efficient use of sheet space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow sheets and diagrams as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow sheets and diagrams may be considered drawings provided they serve as an aid to clear understanding of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphical process diagrams are acceptable if they clarify the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection for IPOPHL E-Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule only one view of each invention can be shown in the IPOPHL E-Gazette illustrations; the selected view must show the nature of the invention or specific improvement; Examiner selects perspective, plan, side or sectional view as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear preferred view(s) so Examiner can choose suitable illustration for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference signs not mentioned in description and claims shall not appear in drawings and vice versa. The same features must be denoted by the same signs throughout. If many reference signs exist, attach a separate sheet listing them with features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict one-to-one correspondence between descriptive text and drawing reference signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are not normally proper drawings but acceptable for obtaining filing date and considered informal drawings. Online photos must be clear and preferably black-and-white; colored allowed if colors clarify. Manually filed black-and-white photographs/photomicrographs acceptable when invention cannot be accurately depicted by ink drawings, provided they comply with printing and paper quality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographs only when necessary and ensure high quality and compliance with reproduction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters not permitted on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent/attorney stamp, advertisement, or written address not permitted on drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep drawings free of extraneous text or stamps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional acceptance of non-conforming drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A drawing not conforming to rules may be admitted for examination if it sufficiently illustrates the invention, but must be corrected or a new one furnished before allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-conforming drawings may allow examination to proceed but correct before grant to avoid refusal at allowance stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets of sequence listing must be numbered 'sheet/total' and independent from other numbering; sequence listing may be submitted as PDF on CD-ROM when manually filed application contains sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow numbering conventions and provide electronic sequence listing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims requirements (form and support)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must conclude with a claim particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the part, improvement or combination regarded as the invention. Application may contain one or more independent claims in same category (product/process/apparatus/use) where appropriate. Each claim shall be clear, concise, and supported by the description. Dependent claims may further limit another claim; multiple dependent claims have special treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft clear independent claims each defining a single inventive concept per category; ensure support in description and permissible dependent claim formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse information (utility model and industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: From date of publication of the utility model or industrial design application, any person may present written adverse information with payment of required fees concerning registrability including novelty and industrial applicability citing relevant prior art. Only properly filed adverse information shall be considered. Office will notify parties of decision. Adverse information must be in form of sworn statement substantiated by evidence and may attach a registrability report. Non-compliant submissions will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse submissions must be sworn, substantiated, and accompanied by fees; the Office may request conferences and accept supplemental adverse information within prescribed timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse information conference and supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested party may request a conference at filing of adverse information, indicating three possible dates within 30 days. Office may request additional info; within 10 days after conference parties may file supplemental adverse information as a sworn statement to include new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conference mechanism to clarify and supplement adverse information; adhere to scheduling and supplemental filing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's comment on adverse information
rubrics_metrics.description: All adverse information is communicated to applicant who may comment within 30 days from mailing date of the communication. Copies of adverse information and comments become part of the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should promptly review and respond to adverse information to preserve record and enable consideration by Examiner/Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision of the Director on registrability (utility model/industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall decide whether to register the utility model or industrial design, may issue registrability report motu proprio. If prior art defeats registrability Director may deny registration or direct applicant to amend/supplement application. Amended applications shall be re-published prior to registration. If Director refuses, applicant may appeal to Director General per IP Code; no motion for reconsideration allowed. If Director allows registration, interested parties may file cancellation petitions under applicable IP Code sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Director's directions for amendments; be aware of appeal routes and post-registration cancellation options. Amendments may trigger re-publication and further adverse input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration without adverse information
rubrics_metrics.description: If application meets formal registrability requirements and no adverse information is received after 30-day publication period, Director shall decide whether to register and may issue registrability report. If registrability report shows prior art defeat, Director may deny or direct amendment. For industrial designs Director may request additional views/drawings to show difference over prior art. If no relevant prior art cited, Office grants registration and informs applicant and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even absent external adverse information, Office may issue registrability report and take action; be prepared to amend if registrability report raises objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of certificate of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate shall be issued in the name of the Republic of the Philippines under the seal of the Office, signed by the Director, and registered together with the description, claims and drawings in Office records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate formalities include registration of core patent documents; maintain file copies consistent with certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of registered documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may inspect the complete description, claims and drawings on file. Marginal notes and exchanges between applicant and Office are not included. Inspection by other international IP offices governed by agreements between Office and those offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public has access to core published documents; internal examiner notes may be withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment/surrender/correction/amendments recordal
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on recording assignment of letters patent and other instruments affecting title, including licenses; surrender, correction, and amendments of patent; recordal and assignment and transmission of rights as provided in Part 12 for patents shall apply mutatis mutandis to utility models and industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Part 12 procedures for changes in ownership/title and certificate corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request a registrability report (utility model/industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant or any interested party, including judicial and quasi-judicial agencies where related case is pending, may request a registrability report upon full payment of required fee. Judicial/quasi-judicial agencies requesting report are exempt from fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrability reports are available to interested parties for due-diligence and litigation support; fee-exemptions apply to certain agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motu proprio issuance of registrability report
rubrics_metrics.description: Director may motu proprio issue a registrability report to assist in determination of registrability; applicant not required to pay a fee in such instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office-initiated registrability reports can be issued without fee to aid decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and scope of registrability report
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrability report shall contain citations of relevant prior art documents with indications as to degree of relevance to aid determination of validity with respect to newness; indicate range of search including relevant prior art publicly known/used anywhere or printed/electronically made available before filing/priority date. Prior art publicly known/used must be supported by affidavit. Registrability reports issued prior to publication shall be published together with the application. Subsequent registrability reports may be requested to include later-found information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should provide helpful prior art context and be supported by affidavit where based on public use/knowledge; can be updated by request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for registrability report issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrability report shall be given within two (2) months from receipt of request with full payment of required fee; may be issued faster in urgent cases upon expedited request with full payment for expedited issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requestors can pay for expedited service; otherwise expect two-month turnaround.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions and appeals procedures applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on petitions and appeals as provided in Part 13 (Rules 1300–1311) of the Regulations for Patents shall apply mutatis mutandis to utility models and industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Part 13 timelines and procedures for petitions and appeals in these domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence with the Office (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: All business with the Office shall be transacted in writing and based exclusively on the written record. Correspondences, responses to Office Actions, reports and other documents shall be submitted/ filed via IPOPHL electronic document submission portal; date of receipt deemed date received by Office electronic system or when payment verified for paid correspondences. Office's issuances shall be sent through IPOPHL electronic correspondence portal; date of mailing is date sent out of Office's electronic system. Enrollment in the electronic correspondence portal is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral promises are disregarded; use electronic portals and enroll to receive/send official correspondence. Non-electronic submissions may be restricted or subject to additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal attendance and addressing correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, personal attendance unnecessary; business can be transacted by correspondence. All Office letters regarding Bureau of Patents matters must be sent in the name of the Director of Patents; letters/communications must be addressed to the Director. A separate letter should be written for each distinct subject. Letters concerning an application must state applicant name, title, and application number. Letters concerning granted patents/registrations must state patentee name, title, patent/registration number and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe address and formality requirements for correspondence to avoid misrouting or return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects on which Office will not give information in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office cannot respond to inquiries as to inventiveness or novelty of an alleged invention or novelty of a utility model/industrial design in advance of filing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect pre-filing substantive determinations from Office; consult counsel or file an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reckoning date for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The date to act on any requests submitted to the Office is the date when complete requirements are submitted and all required fees are fully paid. Requests are not actionable until requirements and payments are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure completeness and payment to start official timelines; partial submissions do not trigger Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees and prepayment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees (filing, publication, annual, etc.) shall be paid through IPOPHL electronic payment facility or electronic document portal, subject to rules and circulars. Express charges, freight, postage, telephone, telefacsimile, cost of paper and other related expenses and all other charges on matters sent to the Office must be prepaid in full; otherwise Office shall not receive nor perform action. Filing fees and other fees payable to the Office collected in advance of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepay all associated charges to avoid rejection/refusal to act on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation, repeals, separability and effectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules shall be implemented by concerned examining and administrative divisions; inconsistent earlier rules/regulations/memoranda are repealed; if any provision held invalid remainder not affected; rules take effect 15 days after publication in newspaper of general circulation and copies furnished to Administrative Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the effective date and that these rules supersede prior inconsistent instruments.
